contract_change_assessment.necessity: The predecessor demands a finite closed interval with tight endpoints for an unrestricted nonzero dimension. At d=1, Φ=I and ρ(x)=I for every real x, so no answer can prove that universal finite-interval assertion. The successor explicitly assesses/refutes it, includes d=1, and retains the sharp nontrivial-dimensional positivity problem instead of silently adding d≥2.
contract_change_assessment.scope: Only question changes in the exact nine-field contract. Both assumption/convention lists remain empty; all real x and every dimension compatible with a rank-one trace-one Φ remain in scope. substantive_reconstruction.trace_and_sectors: Writing P=Φ and Q=I−P gives orthogonal projectors and ρ=aP+bQ, where a=1−x+x/d² and b=x/d². Its trace is (1−x)trP+(x/d²)trI=1 for every real x. For d≥2 the P sector has rank one and Q has rank d²−1, so both coefficients are actual eigenvalues, with their indicated multiplicities (coinciding at x=1).
substantive_reconstruction.sharp_range: Positive semidefiniteness for d≥2 is equivalent to a,b≥0, hence exactly 0≤x≤d²/(d²−1). Necessity has concrete witnesses: a unit vector |1,2⟩ is orthogonal to Φ+ and has expectation b<0 when x<0; Φ+ has expectation a<0 beyond the upper endpoint. These also prove both endpoints tight, not merely sufficient. At x=0 the state is Φ of rank one; at the upper endpoint it is (I−Φ)/(d²−1), of rank d²−1.
substantive_reconstruction.degenerate_dimensions: For d=1 the complementary projector Q is zero. The coefficient b=x multiplies a rank-zero sector and is not an eigenvalue constraint; a=1 and the sole state is I for every x, including negative values. The allowed set is all R, without finite positivity endpoints. Dimension zero was already incompatible with the stipulated rank-one trace-one maximally entangled projector and is not being newly excluded to repair the theorem. Positivity here says nothing about separability or PPT.

answer_rubric_and_exposition_assessment: The four rubric criteria require the d=1 refutation rather than rewarding an implicit restriction, trace and genuine sector multiplicities, necessary-and-sufficient interval with negativity witnesses, and endpoint ranks/degenerate boundaries. The full exposition has the same three ordered support lists and correctly treats a zero-rank sector. The answer does not confuse coefficients with distinct eigenvalues when x=1, or positivity with an entanglement threshold. Thus the entire candidate, including grading and boundaries, is mathematically acceptable as an explicit first question-version2 correction.
